Good. I have enough now. Let me synthesize what I can see across the project and the conversation record before producing anything. Here's what I found — and the inconsistencies that need addressing before tomorrow.

Review: v5 State vs. Built Materials

What v5 locked

From the June 6 synthesis session, the confirmed spine:

Structure: Opening → Lightning Round → Interrogate (data) → Interpret (text) → Iterate (own artifact) → Wrap

Bookends: "Who prompted that?" / "It is worth exactly what you put into it."

Three verbs live in the slides — no separate handout

Participants identified by number, corresponding to row in shared Google Doc (not color cards)

Round 2: single model — the two-model hand-off was dropped

Round 3: Iteration, not Validation — this was explicitly rejected on 6/4

Base path: one model, share link; everything richer is optional

Inconsistencies between v5 and the published workshop.html

Three discrepancies in the live site:

1. Round 3 framing — serious. The infrastructure block in workshop.html says:

"Gemini free (primary — all rounds); Claude free (Round 3 validation)"

"Validation" is the exact framing v5 rejected. If participants read this before the room, it primes the wrong expectation. Should read "iteration" or simply "Round 3 polish".

2. Round 2 description — significant. The verb card for Round 2 reads:

"One model reads it and produces an artifact. A second reads the artifact. You decide what each one missed."

The second model was dropped in v5. The description is still running the old two-model design. If facilitating from the site as a reference, this is a source of confusion.

3. Round 3 verb card description — minor but worth noting. Currently:

"Take your best work from Rounds 1 and 2. Hand it to a fresh model. Push back, refine, again — until it sounds like you wrote it."

The phrase "until it sounds like you wrote it" is actually fine and survives v5 — this one is clean.

Holes still open in v5 (bracketed, not resolved)

Round 1 lesson line. You rejected "ask the data / curiosity" and no replacement was locked. The deck has a [VERIFY: lesson phrase] placeholder.

Round 3 phrase from "learner's permit, lesson fourteen." You referenced an external document that holds the language you want. Never recovered.

The talk (June 9) is unbuilt. The universal-vs-leveled literacy contradiction between the submitted synopsis and the locked argument was flagged but not resolved before the talk was built.

The design spec question

You mentioned "design specs" and "similar document set" in relation to the cowork files. I can see from the project record that the cowork spec structure produced: facilitator deck, participant reference card, system prompt library, scenario inventory, and round-specific documents. That architecture is worth replicating for Farmingdale and for any other context.

But I need one answer before I produce anything: what is the design spec for?

The candidates I can see from the project horizon:

The June 9 talk (most urgent — two days away)

The Manufacturing Workforce Development Forum at SUNY Farmingdale (date unspecified)

A generalizable workshop spec that can travel to other professional audiences (HIM → manufacturing → agriculture → etc.)

Something else

Once you tell me the target, I'll produce the spec with the design system (DM Serif Display / DM Sans / JetBrains Mono, navy/crimson/gold/cream) and the tone you described — agency over adaptation, the weight of 25,000 years of tool-use history, economic and environmental honesty, no cheerleading.

And before I do anything else: do you want me to push the two fixes to workshop.html right now? The Round 3 "validation" language and the Round 2 second-model description are both wrong and the workshop is tomorrow.
